I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` workflow because this is a scan-driven investigation. I’ll validate the relevant source around the high-severity drift, then distinguish the reported plan-validation bug from the separate route issues.

The skill file isn’t present at the repository-relative path advertised in the environment, so I’m locating the actual checkout boundary before continuing. This is only a read-only investigation; I won’t alter the fixture.

The global `crimes` binary is not installed in this evaluation shell, but the supplied JSON is consistent with the source: Python’s canonical enum includes `scale`, while the TypeScript union does not. I also confirmed there are independent path/method mismatches; they can break requests, but they are not the web-only plan validation error described.

The root cause is duplicated, hand-maintained plan definitions that have drifted across languages:

- The API’s Python `Plan` enum accepts `free`, `pro`, `team`, and `scale` in [plans.py](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10).
- The web client’s TypeScript `Plan` only permits `free`, `pro`, and `enterprise` in [workspace-client.ts](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/729ccd5a-2231-4f76-9c65-0487f212a072/scratchpad/eval-wt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10).

Consequently, the newest `scale` plan is valid to the API but outside the web app’s closed set, so frontend validation rejects it before—or while—interpreting the API data. `team` has the same problem, while `enterprise` has the inverse problem: the web recognizes it but the canonical API enum does not.

The durable fix is to maintain one canonical contract and generate the other representation from it—for example, publish the Python enum through OpenAPI or a shared JSON Schema and generate the TypeScript client/types. Add a CI contract test or code-generation freshness check so mismatched plan sets fail before merging.

There is also a separate request bug: the web uses `PUT` for the plan endpoint while the backend declares `POST`, which can produce a 405 after validation is fixed. That route contract should likewise be generated or tested from the same API specification.
